title: Two days before the last day of the six months

expect.why: «في أجل لا يتجاوز ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح»: delivery 2025-12-10 plus six months gives 2026-06-10 (a Wednesday). 2026-06-08 is before the last day under every reading of how the days are counted (last day 2026-06-09, 06-10 or 06-11), so it is in time.

title: The day before the last day of the six months

expect.why: «ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح»: six months from 2025-12-10 end on 2026-06-10. 2026-06-09 is one day before. Even if the starting day were counted (last day 2026-06-09) the petition is still in time, so every reading agrees.

title: Filed on the day the six months expire by the calendar

expect.why: The text does not settle this: «ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح» does not say whether the day of delivery counts, nor whether the last day is included. Reading 1 (starting day excluded, period complete at the end of its last day): last day 2026-06-10, so the petition is on the last day. Reading 2 (starting day counted): last day 2026-06-09, so it is late. Reading 3 (neither first nor last day counted): last day 2026-06-11. The more likely reading is the first, last day 2026-06-10. A rule must warn, not decide.

title: Filed the day after the calendar anniversary of the delivery

expect.why: The text does not settle this: the texts given contain no rule of counting days or months. Last day 2026-06-10 (starting day excluded): the petition is one day late and the right is forfeited («تحت طائلة سقوط الحق في رفع الدعوى»). Last day 2026-06-11 (neither first nor last day counted): it is on the last day and in time. Both last days are plausible, so a rule must warn, not decide.

title: Five days after the last day of the six months

expect.why: «أجل لا يتجاوز ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح ... تحت طائلة سقوط الحق»: last day 2026-06-10; the longest plausible last day is 2026-06-11 and none of 06-10, 06-11 falls on a rest day (a Wednesday, a Thursday), so 2026-06-15 is late under every reading. Outside any warning band of a few days.

title: Six months end on a Friday; petition on the Sunday after

expect.why: Delivery 2025-12-12 plus six months ends on 2026-06-12, a Friday. The texts given do not say which days are days of weekly rest, and contain no rule that a period ending on a rest day runs to the next working day, so the text does not settle this. Reading 1: last day 2026-06-12, the petition of Sunday 2026-06-14 is late. Reading 2 (a rest day extends the period): the last day moves to the next working day, which is Sunday 2026-06-14 if Friday and Saturday are rest days, and the petition is on the last day. I give 2026-06-12 as last day because the texts given contain no extension rule. A rule must warn, not decide.

title: Six months end on 5 July, an official holiday and a Sunday

expect.why: Delivery 2026-01-05 plus six months ends on 2026-07-05 (a Sunday). The texts given list no official holidays and no weekly rest days, and no article of them extends a period that ends on such a day, so the text does not settle this. Last day 2026-07-05: the petition of 2026-07-06 is one day late. If the period runs to the next working day, or the last day is not counted, the last day is 2026-07-06 and the petition is in time. A rule must warn, not decide.

title: Delivery on 31 August: the sixth month, February, has no 31st

expect.why: «ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح»: six months from 31 August 2025 lands in February 2026, which has 28 days (2026 is not a leap year). The text does not settle this: it does not say what a month period does when the day number is missing. Reading 1: the period ends on the last day of the month, 2026-02-28 (a Saturday), so a petition of Sunday 2026-03-01 is late. Reading 2: the missing days overflow, giving 2026-03-03, so it is in time. A rule must warn, not decide.

title: Delivery on 31 December: June has no 31st; petition on 1 July

expect.why: «ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح»: six months from 31 December 2025 lands in June 2026, which has 30 days. The text does not settle how a month period ending in a shorter month is counted. Reading 1: it ends on 2026-06-30 (a Tuesday), so the petition of 2026-07-01 is late. Reading 2: 31 June is read as 1 July, so the petition is on the last day. A rule must warn, not decide.

title: Delivery on 29 August: February 28 is the exact sixth-month day, petition well before

expect.why: «ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح»: 2025-08-29 plus six months is 2026-02-28 (February 2026 has 28 days, not a leap year; the 29th would not exist, so a rule that adds six months to day 29 of a month and lands in February must not mistake it). 2026-02-20 is eight days before, in time under every reading.

title: Petition long before the limit

expect.why: «ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح»: 2026-02-02 plus six months is 2026-08-02; the petition is five months and more before it, far outside any warning band.

title: Petition filed more than a year after the record

expect.why: «في أجل لا يتجاوز ستة (6) أشهر ... تحت طائلة سقوط الحق في رفع الدعوى»: 2025-09-15 plus six months is 2026-03-15; the petition is six months after that, far late under any reading.

title: Starting event: record drawn 10 December but delivered on 18 December

expect.why: The time runs «من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح», the delivery of the record, not its drawing. The record was drawn on 2025-12-10 (a date no slot holds) and delivered on 2025-12-18. From the delivery the last day is 2026-06-18 and 2026-06-15 is in time under every reading. A rule that started the count at the date of the record (last day 2026-06-10) would call it late.

title: Petition filed on the very day the record is delivered

expect.why: «أجل لا يتجاوز ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح»: delivery 2026-03-02, last day 2026-09-02. A petition on the day of delivery is six months before the last day, in time. [labour-disputes 30 ¶2] «تسلم نسخة من المحضر الى المدعي اثناء الاجتماع» shows delivery can be the meeting day itself.

title: Record of non-conciliation obtained, delivery date not known

expect.why: The record exists, so the step of [labour-disputes 19 ¶1] is taken, but the time runs «من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح» and the delivery date is unknown, so the last day cannot be computed: the rule must ask for it, not assume the date of the record or the petition.

title: Conciliation step: the record exists, delivered in time

expect.why: «يجب أن يكون كل خلاف فردي خاص بالعمل موضوع محاولة للصلح أمام مكتب المصالحة قبل مباشرة أي دعوى قضائية» and [labour-disputes 37 ¶1] «ترفق العريضة ... بنسخة من محضر عدم المصالحة»: a record of non-conciliation was drawn and delivered on 2026-04-01, so the step is done, and nothing about its means or date is still open (the petition is a month later).

title: Conciliation step: whether a record was drawn is not known

expect.why: «قبل مباشرة أي دعوى قضائية»: whether the step was done is unknown, and an unknown fact is never a no. The rule must ask the lawyer for the record, not decide that the step is missing.

title: Conciliation step not taken, no exemption known to apply

expect.why: «يجب أن يكون كل خلاف فردي خاص بالعمل موضوع محاولة للصلح أمام مكتب المصالحة قبل مباشرة أي دعوى قضائية»: no record, and the party is not a public body. The other exemptions of [labour-disputes 19 ¶2] (defendant abroad, employer bankrupt or in judicial settlement) and the civil-servant exclusion of ¶3 have no slot; this case assumes none applies. The text gives no sanction for skipping the step, but the lawyer must be shown it is missing; [labour-disputes 37 ¶1] requires the record to be attached.

title: Conciliation step not taken, a public administrative body is a party

expect.why: The text does not settle this. «ويستثنى من مجال اختصاص مكاتب المصالحة الخلافات الفردية للعمل التي يكون طرفا فيها الموظفون والأعوان الخاضعون للقانون الأساسي للمؤسسات والإدارات العمومية» excludes civil servants and public agents under the public-service statute, not every worker of a public body: a contract worker of a public administrative body may still have to go to the conciliation office. The slot says only that a party is a public administrative body, not that the worker is under the public-service statute, and the texts given do not say whether such a dispute leaves the ordinary courts. A rule must warn, not decide.

title: Just inside the ordinary courts: the employer is a public company

expect.why: A public company is not «الدولة أو ولاية أو بلدية أو مؤسسة عمومية ذات طابع إداري», so public_body_party is no. [labour-disputes 20 ¶2] sends individual labour disputes to the social section, and the exclusion of ¶3 reaches only civil servants and agents under the public-service statute. The case stays in the ordinary courts, conciliation is required and was not done (other exemptions have no slot and are assumed absent).
